topic: The Pi-Collision Mystery: From Physics to Mathematics

outline.topic: The Pi-Collision Mystery: From Physics to Mathematics

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Elastic Collision Paradox
sections.content: Introduce a 1D elastic collision scenario between two blocks of different masses. Explain that when the mass ratio is a power of 100 (M = 100^n * m), the number of total collisions perfectly maps to the digits of pi.
sections.example: A small block (mass 1kg) moves toward a large block (mass 100kg) which is resting against a wall. The small block bounces off the large one and the wall repeatedly.

sections.title: Visualizing the Phase Space
sections.content: Represent the system as a particle moving in a 2D plane (billiard ball model). Use a graphical 'unfolding' technique: instead of bouncing, the particle travels in a straight line through reflections in a configuration space defined by x and y axes.
sections.example: An animation showing a particle moving at an angle θ in a triangular potential well, where the angle is determined by the ratio of the masses.

sections.title: The Geometric Connection to Pi
sections.content: Explain why the number of collisions is exactly the number of times the line hits the 'boundary' of the phase space. The total path length is proportional to the arc length of a circle, connecting the dynamics of the blocks to the geometry of π.
sections.example: An animation transforming the 'bouncing' motion into a straight-line trajectory across a grid, where the path crosses lines at coordinates corresponding to the digits 3, 1, 4, 1, 5...

sections.title: Application and Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize that as the mass ratio grows (100^n), the system acts as a physical 'computer' calculating digits of pi. This demonstrates how simple conservation of momentum and energy laws can produce deeply complex mathematical constants.
sections.example: A final visual showing a massive block (10,000kg) resulting in a longer sequence of collisions, counting out the first 4 digits of Pi (3, 1, 4, 1) as the blocks rhythmically bounce.

Reflections correspond to specific digits of Pi.
animations: Display unit circle to represent normalized energy constraints.
Animate: Count the number of total reflections in trajectory.
Overlay: Show pi digits corresponding to reflection sequence.
